input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: an optional argument's metavar is wrapped in brackets without checking whether the type already bracketed it
- failure path: an optional Choice argument renders in the usage line as [[foo|bar|baz]] with two pairs of brackets instead of [foo|bar|baz]

Reviewer finding
- description: The `already_bracketed` guard was removed from `make_metavar`, so an optional argument whose type metavar is already bracketed now gets bracketed a second time.
- rationale: Trigger: an optional Argument (required=False) whose type's get_metavar returns a bracketed string, e.g. a custom ParamType or Choice-like metavar such as "[a|b]". The old code skipped wrapping when the metavar was already bracketed. The new code always wraps it, so usage text shows "[[a|b]]". Users see malformed help and usage output. Because the check was deliberately present, this is likely an unintended regression.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. make_metavar wraps an optional argument's metavar in brackets without checking whether it is already bracketed, so a Choice-like metavar renders as [[a|b]].
